contracts: Accepted incoming connection children are owned by a lexical JoinSet from initial handshake through H3 bootstrap, first/partial HEADERS, rejection wait and full active relay; owner abort drops that set.
ProxyEndpoint drop explicitly closes endpoint connections; mere Endpoint drop is not used as proof of existing connection teardown.

CloseState generation snapshot is taken in accepting owner before spawning child; close increments generation, reopen clears closed flag without rolling generation back. Existing children see a mismatch even when watch true/false collapses before their next poll.

Before authenticated connection exists, close cancels the incoming future; after it exists, whole serve_connected future is selected against generation, covering nested awaits rather than relay loop edges.

Final ProxyConnection guard drop precedes pinned H3 future destruction on cancellation. Established protocol errors remain first close reason because Quinn proto close_inner does not overwrite an already-closed state.

Completed child results/JoinErrors are stored and available through take_failures. The added duplicate-control-stream control observes actual remote code0x103 and downcasts exactly one retained Local H3_STREAM_CREATION_ERROR, rather than inferring recovery from ownership.

Relay send/receive failures propagate; explicit unknown context/stream datagrams still skipped and the existing Windows ConnectionReset allowance remains. Rejection wait accepts only actual stream end or explicit remote QUIC applicationclose0, not arbitrary errors.

Private concrete guards are owner-local and have distinct responsibilities; no generic task framework or unrelated module split. Loopback UDP uses existing retrying helper; TLS settings/MTU/pseudo-header order unchanged.
